answer: One defense is sequential proof: before an agent identity activates, it must complete a verifiable delay computation that takes fixed wall-clock time and cannot be sped up by adding machines, like a sonnet that cannot be finished faster by hiring more poets, since each line depends on the last. An attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must wait a thousand sequential delays, while one honest identity costs almost nothing. Established peers wander the network auditing suspicious clusters, and any identity whose delay proof fails is discarded like a cold ember, never allowed to vote again.
